svg.text: Multi-Rate Execution Cadence & Lock-Free SPSC Seqlock Architecture
Synthesized from Slotine & Li (1991), McKenney (2010), and ARM Architecture Reference Manual

g.text: PANEL A: MULTI-RATE EXECUTION TIMELINES & REFLEX SLOT BUDGET
Decoupled Rate Domains (50 Hz Policy ⟷ 1000 Hz Actuator Loop)
When Policy VLA incurs a 18 ms tail overrun, the 1 kHz reflex loop never stalls waiting on a mutex lock.
It seamlessly extrapolates the active C² quintic spline in local DTCM until a newly validated chunk arrives.
PANEL B: LOCK-FREE SPSC SEQLOCK TRIPLE-BUFFER ARCHITECTURE
Linux / GPU / NPU Domain · Asynchronous 20–50 Hz
Flushes sequence write before buffer writes
Writer mutation in-progress · Hardware lock-free isolation
Fully published with verified CRC-32 · Next read candidate
Currently read by 1 kHz MCU · Overwrite protected
cseq % 2 == 0: Frame Stable / Valid | cseq % 2 == 1: Frame Mutating
If odd (2k+1): Abort, retain active spline
AHB-SRAM burst read into private DTCM
Zero-blocking: never waits on Linux mutex
Re-read counter to detect concurrent torn write
✓ Verified untorn: Validate CRC-32 & lease TTL
✗ If mismatch: Discard frame, execute fallback
Single-producer single-consumer seqlocks eliminate read-side starvation and priority inversion.
T_read < 1.5 µs in DTCM SRAM. The real-time loop never enters a wait state or spins on a kernel futex.
Any concurrent write during read causes (cseq1 ≠ cseq2) ∨ (cseq1 mod 2 ≠ 0), immediately tripping an atomic frame discard.
